text:
mike: Noticed linkcheck is failing on anchors created from numbered list headings after the migration. e.g. headings like `1. Setup (quick)` end up with different slugs in MkDocs vs Docusaurus.
tasha: saw that too. paste from CI: 
```
[linkcheck] WARNING: ./guides/setup.mdx: anchor not found: 1-setup-quick
[linkcheck] WARNING: ./howto/paths.mdx: anchor not found: setup-1-advanced
```
rui: quick repro locally: mkdocs strips leading list numbers when computing slugs but docusaurus preserves them or swaps punctuation. Also parentheses and trailing periods are treated inconsistently.
mike: this is annoying because a lot of our legacy docs use numbered headings for step sequences. We should avoid changing visible content but make slugs stable across toolchains.
tasha: two options: 1) add automatic slug aliases in frontmatter (heavy touch, large PR), or 2) run a conservative heading-only normalizer in CI that canonicalizes leading list numbers and punctuation strictly for slug generation (preferred).
rui: i'd vote sanitizer in docs-ci: only touch heading lines (start with #) and do: remove leading list numbers like `^\s*\d+\.\s+`, replace `(` and `)` with nothing for slugging, collapse punctuation runs, and map curly quotes/ellipsis as usual. keep body intact.
mike: agree. can you sketch the one-liner?
rui: perl example for CI step (heading-only):
```bash
perl -C -0777 -pe "s/(?m)^\s*#\s*(\d+\.\s+)//g; s/\x{2026}/.../g; s/[\x{2018}\x{2019}]/'/g; s/[\x{201C}\x{201D}]/\"/g; s/[\x{200B}-\x{200D}\x{FEFF}\x{00AD}]//g; s/(?m)^(#\s*)([^\n]+)/\$1.(my $h=$2)=~s/[^\w\- ]//gr =~ s/\s{2,}/ /gr/ger;" -i "$f"
```
mike: hmm that one-liner is a bit dense; maybe keep the script small and readable. add dry-run mode so infra can preview.
tasha: i'll open a PR that adds a small `scripts/normalize_headings.sh` which runs a heading-only sanitizer and a node-based slug-compare test that runs both slugifiers against samples. PR will include migration note and test vectors.
ci-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1928 by tasha (adds heading normalizer + slug-compare test + migration note). CI queued.
doc-bot: tip: encourage editors to avoid visible leading numbers in headings; use ordered lists instead. But we can still normalize for migration compatibility. :memo:
ci-bot: CI passed for PR #1928 (linkcheck + docs-lint + tests).
tasha: merged. eng-infra: can you run a non-destructive backfill to apply the sanitizer across main? prefer single maintenance commit if possible.
eng-infra: will run a dry-run first, then apply as a single commit by infra-bot. scheduling T+30m.
eng-infra: dry-run complete: 21 files would be modified. proceeding with single maintenance commit.
eng-infra: backfill applied: 21 files modified, commit "docs: normalize heading numbering and punctuation to stabilize anchors" pushed by infra-bot. linkcheck on main now green.
mike: awesome. tasha/rui thanks for the quick patch and tests. i'll add a short note to the contributor guide advising against numbered headings to prevent future surprises.
tasha: added a PR to the contributors doc. closing this thread after the contributor guide PR merges. :white_check_mark:
